# dtgsja

> Computes the generalized singular value decomposition (GSVD) of two real upper triangular (or trapezoidal) matrices A and B.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dtgsja from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dtgsja';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dtgsja(
    order,
    jobu, jobv, jobq,
    M, p, N,
    K, l,
    A, LDA,
    B, LDB,
    tola, tolb,
    ALPHA, strideALPHA,
    BETA, strideBETA,
    U, LDU,
    V, LDV,
    Q, LDQ,
    WORK,
    ncycle
) → integer
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | Storage layout ('row-major' or 'column-major') |
| `jobu` | `"update" \| "initialize" \| "none"` | `'compute-vectors'`: U must contain an orthogonal matrix U1 on entry, and the product U1\*U is returned; `'initialize'`: U is initialized to the unit matrix, and the orthogonal matrix U is returned; `'none'`: U is not computed.<br>One of `'initialize'`, `'none'`, `'update'`. |
| `jobv` | `"update" \| "initialize" \| "none"` | `'compute-vectors'`: V must contain an orthogonal matrix V1 on entry, and the product V1\*V is returned; `'initialize'`: V is initialized to the unit matrix, and the orthogonal matrix V is returned; `'none'`: V is not computed.<br>One of `'initialize'`, `'none'`, `'update'`. |
| `jobq` | `"update" \| "initialize" \| "none"` | `'compute-vectors'`: Q must contain an orthogonal matrix Q1 on entry, and the product Q1\*Q is returned; `'initialize'`: Q is initialized to the unit matrix, and the orthogonal matrix Q is returned; `'none'`: Q is not computed.<br>One of `'initialize'`, `'none'`, `'update'`. |
| `M` | `NonNegativeInteger` | The number of rows of the matrix A.<br>Requires `M ≥ 0` |
| `p` | `NonNegativeInteger` | The number of rows of the matrix B.<br>Requires `p ≥ 0` |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | The number of columns of the matrices A and B.<br>Requires `N ≥ 0` |
| `K` | `integer` | K and L specify the subblocks in the input matrices A and B: A23 = A(K+1:MIN(K+L,M),N-L+1:N) and B13 = B(1:L,N-L+1:N) of A and B, whose GSVD is going to be computed by DTGSJA. |
| `l` | `integer` | K and L specify the subblocks in the input matrices A and B: A23 = A(K+1:MIN(K+L,M),N-L+1:N) and B13 = B(1:L,N-L+1:N) of A and B, whose GSVD is going to be computed by DTGSJA. |
| `A` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>M × N</sub> | **in/out** · On entry, the M-by-N matrix A. On exit, A(N-K+1:N,1:MIN(K+L,M) ) contains the triangular matrix R or part of R. |
| ↳ `LDA` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `A`<br>Column-major requires `LDA ≥ max(1, M)`<br>Row-major requires `LDA ≥ max(1, N)` |
| `B` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>P × N</sub> | **in/out** · On entry, the P-by-N matrix B. On exit, if necessary, B(M-K+1:L,N+M-K-L+1:N) contains a part of R. |
| ↳ `LDB` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `B`<br>Column-major requires `LDB ≥ max(1, P)`<br>Row-major requires `LDB ≥ max(1, N)` |
| `tola` | `number` | TOLA and TOLB are the convergence criteria for the Jacobi- Kogbetliantz iteration procedure. |
| `tolb` | `number` | TOLA and TOLB are the convergence criteria for the Jacobi- Kogbetliantz iteration procedure. |
| `ALPHA` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **out** · On exit, ALPHA and BETA contain the generalized singular value pairs of A and B. |
| ↳ `strideALPHA` | `integer` | Stride length for `ALPHA` |
| `BETA` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **out** · On exit, ALPHA and BETA contain the generalized singular value pairs of A and B. |
| ↳ `strideBETA` | `integer` | Stride length for `BETA` |
| `U` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>M × M</sub> | **in/out** · On entry, if `jobu === 'compute-vectors'`, U must contain a matrix U1 (usually the orthogonal matrix returned by DGGSVP). On exit, if `jobu === 'initialize'`, U contains the orthogonal matrix U; if `jobu === 'compute-vectors'`, U contains the product U1\*U. |
| ↳ `LDU` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `U`<br>Rejects `ldu < 1 \|\| ((jobu === 'initialize' \|\| jobu === 'update') && ldu < M)` |
| `V` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>P × P</sub> | **in/out** · On entry, if `jobv === 'compute-vectors'`, V must contain a matrix V1 (usually the orthogonal matrix returned by DGGSVP). On exit, if `jobv === 'initialize'`, V contains the orthogonal matrix V; if `jobv === 'compute-vectors'`, V contains the product V1\*V. |
| ↳ `LDV` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `V`<br>Rejects `ldv < 1 \|\| ((jobv === 'initialize' \|\| jobv === 'update') && ldv < P)` |
| `Q` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | **in/out** · On entry, if `jobq === 'compute-vectors'`, Q must contain a matrix Q1 (usually the orthogonal matrix returned by DGGSVP). On exit, if `jobq === 'initialize'`, Q contains the orthogonal matrix Q; if `jobq === 'compute-vectors'`, Q contains the product Q1\*Q. |
| ↳ `LDQ` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `Q`<br>Rejects `ldq < 1 \|\| ((jobq === 'initialize' \|\| jobq === 'update') && ldq < N)` |
| `WORK` | `Float64Array \| null`<br><sub>length ≥ 2 * N</sub> | **out** · Caller-provided workspace of at least `2 * N` elements |
| `ncycle` | `Int32Array` | **out** · The number of cycles required for convergence. |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `jobu`:

  -   `= 'U'`: U must contain an orthogonal matrix U1 on entry, and the product $U_{1} \, U$ is returned;
  -   `= 'I'`: U is initialized to the unit matrix, and the orthogonal matrix U is returned;
  -   `= 'N'`: U is not computed.
- `jobv`:

  -   `= 'V'`: V must contain an orthogonal matrix V1 on entry, and the product $V_{1} \, V$ is returned;
  -   `= 'I'`: V is initialized to the unit matrix, and the orthogonal matrix V is returned;
  -   `= 'N'`: V is not computed.
- `jobq`:

  -   `= 'Q'`: Q must contain an orthogonal matrix Q1 on entry, and the product $Q_{1} \, Q$ is returned;
  -   `= 'I'`: Q is initialized to the unit matrix, and the orthogonal matrix Q is returned;
  -   `= 'N'`: Q is not computed.
- `M`: The number of rows of the matrix A. $M \ge 0$.
- `p`: The number of rows of the matrix B. $P \ge 0$.
- `N`: The number of columns of the matrices A and B. $N \ge 0$.
- `l`: K and L specify the subblocks in the input matrices A and B: $A_{23} = A(K+1:\min (K+L,M),N-L+1:N)$ and $B_{13} = B(1:L,N-L+1:N)$ of A and B, whose GSVD is going to be computed by DTGSJA. See Further Details.
- `A`: On entry, the M-by-N matrix A. On exit, A(N-K+1:N,1:MIN(K+L,M) ) contains the triangular matrix R or part of R. See Purpose for details.
- `B`: On entry, the P-by-N matrix B. On exit, if necessary, `B(M-K+1:L,N+M-K-L+1:N)` contains a part of R. See Purpose for details.
- `tolb`: `TOLA` and `TOLB` are the convergence criteria for the Jacobi- Kogbetliantz iteration procedure. Generally, they are the same as used in the preprocessing step, say

  $$
  \mathrm{TOLA} = \max (M,N) \, \operatorname{norm}(A) \, \mathrm{MAZHEPS}
  $$

  $$
  \mathrm{TOLB} = \max (P,N) \, \operatorname{norm}(B) \, \mathrm{MAZHEPS}
  $$
- `BETA`: On exit, `ALPHA` and `BETA` contain the generalized singular value pairs of A and B;

  $$
  \mathrm{ALPHA}(1:K) = 1
  $$

  $$
  \mathrm{BETA}(1:K) = 0
  $$

  and if $M-K-L \ge 0$,

  $$
  \mathrm{ALPHA}(K+1:K+L) = \operatorname{diag}(C)
  $$

  $$
  \mathrm{BETA}(K+1:K+L) = \operatorname{diag}(S)
  $$

  or if $M-K-L < 0$,

  $$
  \mathrm{ALPHA}(K+1:M)= C, \mathrm{ALPHA}(M+1:K+L)= 0
  $$

  $$
  \mathrm{BETA}(K+1:M) = S, \mathrm{BETA}(M+1:K+L) = 1
  $$

  Furthermore, if $K+L < N$,

  $$
  \mathrm{ALPHA}(K+L+1:N) = 0 \quad\text{and}\quad
  $$

  $$
  \mathrm{BETA}(K+L+1:N) = 0
  $$
- `U`: On entry, if `JOBU = 'U'`, U must contain a matrix U1 (usually the orthogonal matrix returned by DGGSVP). On exit, if `JOBU = 'I'`, U contains the orthogonal matrix U; if `JOBU = 'U'`, U contains the product $U_{1} \, U$. If `JOBU = 'N'`, U is not referenced.
- `V`: On entry, if `JOBV = 'V'`, V must contain a matrix V1 (usually the orthogonal matrix returned by DGGSVP). On exit, if `JOBV = 'I'`, V contains the orthogonal matrix V; if `JOBV = 'V'`, V contains the product $V_{1} \, V$. If `JOBV = 'N'`, V is not referenced.
- `Q`: On entry, if `JOBQ = 'Q'`, Q must contain a matrix Q1 (usually the orthogonal matrix returned by DGGSVP). On exit, if `JOBQ = 'I'`, Q contains the orthogonal matrix Q; if `JOBQ = 'Q'`, Q contains the product $Q_{1} \, Q$. If `JOBQ = 'N'`, Q is not referenced.
- `ncycle`: The number of cycles required for convergence.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: info status code

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order
- `TypeError` second argument must be one of the following: "initialize", "none", "update"
- `TypeError` third argument must be one of the following: "initialize", "none", "update"
- `TypeError` fourth argument must be one of the following: "initialize", "none", "update"
- `RangeError` fifth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` sixth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` seventh argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` eleventh argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, M )` (column-major)
- `RangeError` eleventh argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )` (row-major)
- `RangeError` thirteenth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, p )` (column-major)
- `RangeError` thirteenth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )` (row-major)
- `RangeError` twenty-first argument is invalid (rejected when `LDU < 1 \|\| ( ( jobu === "initialize" \|\| jobu === "update" ) && LDU < M )`)
- `RangeError` twenty-third argument is invalid (rejected when `LDV < 1 \|\| ( ( jobv === "initialize" \|\| jobv === "update" ) && LDV < p )`)
- `RangeError` twenty-fifth argument is invalid (rejected when `LDQ < 1 \|\| ( ( jobq === "initialize" \|\| jobq === "update" ) && LDQ < N )`)
- `TypeError` if a string argument is not a valid option

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dtgsja.ndarray(
    jobu, jobv, jobq,
    M, p, N,
    K, l,
    A, strideA1, strideA2, offsetA,
    B, strideB1, strideB2, offsetB,
    tola, tolb,
    ALPHA, strideALPHA, offsetALPHA,
    BETA, strideBETA, offsetBETA,
    U, strideU1, strideU2, offsetU,
    V, strideV1, strideV2, offsetV,
    Q, strideQ1, strideQ2, offsetQ,
    WORK, strideWork, offsetWork,
    ncycle
) → info: integer
```

Computes the generalized singular value decomposition (GSVD) of two real.
upper triangular (or trapezoidal) matrices A and B.

On entry, it is assumed that matrices A and B have the forms obtained by
the preprocessing subroutine DGGSVP.

On exit, U^T_A_Q = D1_(0 R), V^T_B_Q = D2_(0 R), where U, V and Q are
orthogonal matrices.

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `jobu` | `"update" \| "initialize" \| "none"` | `'update'`, `'initialize'`, or `'none'` |
| `jobv` | `"update" \| "initialize" \| "none"` | `'update'`, `'initialize'`, or `'none'` |
| `jobq` | `"update" \| "initialize" \| "none"` | `'update'`, `'initialize'`, or `'none'` |
| `M` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of rows of A<br>Requires `M ≥ 0` |
| `p` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of rows of B<br>Requires `p ≥ 0` |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of columns of A and B<br>Requires `N ≥ 0` |
| `K` | `integer` | Dimension of the first block |
| `l` | `integer` | Dimension of the second block |
| `A` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>M × N</sub> | **in/out** · M-by-N matrix A (overwritten) |
| ↳ `strideA1` | `integer` | Stride of first dimension of A |
| ↳ `strideA2` | `integer` | Stride of second dimension of A |
| ↳ `offsetA` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for A |

- `TypeError` first argument must be one of the following: "initialize", "none", "update"

- `RangeError` fifth argument must be a nonnegative integer

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`.

The reference documents `INFO` as:

-   `= 0`: successful exit
-   `< 0`: if `INFO = -i`, the i-th argument had an illegal value.
-   `= 1`: the procedure does not converge after MAXIT cycles.

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import Int32Array from '@stdlib/array/int32/lib/index.js';
import dtgsja from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dtgsja';

const M = 3;
const p = 3;
const N = 3;
const K = 0;
const l = 3;
const tola = 1.0e-12;
const tolb = 1.0e-12;

// Upper triangular A (M-by-N) and B (p-by-N), as preprocessed by dggsvp3 with K = 0 and l = N (column-major):
let A = new Float64Array( [ 2.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0, 3.0, 0.0, 0.5, 1.0, 4.0 ] );
let B = new Float64Array( [ 1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.5, 2.0, 0.0, 0.2, 0.3, 1.5 ] );
const ALPHA = new Float64Array( N );
const BETA = new Float64Array( N );
const U = new Float64Array( M * M );
const V = new Float64Array( p * p );
const Q = new Float64Array( N * N );
const WORK = new Float64Array( 2 * N );
const ncycle = new Int32Array( 1 );

// Using the standard interface:
let info = dtgsja( 'column-major', 'initialize', 'initialize', 'initialize', M, p, N, K, l, A, M, B, p, tola, tolb, ALPHA, 1, BETA, 1, U, M, V, p, Q, N, WORK, ncycle );
console.log( info ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
console.log( ALPHA ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
console.log( BETA ); // eslint-disable-line no-console

// Using the ndarray interface:
A = new Float64Array( [ 2.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0, 3.0, 0.0, 0.5, 1.0, 4.0 ] );
B = new Float64Array( [ 1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.5, 2.0, 0.0, 0.2, 0.3, 1.5 ] );
info = dtgsja.ndarray( 'initialize', 'initialize', 'initialize', M, p, N, K, l, A, 1, M, 0, B, 1, p, 0, tola, tolb, ALPHA, 1, 0, BETA, 1, 0, U, 1, M, 0, V, 1, p, 0, Q, 1, N, 0, WORK, 1, 0, ncycle );
console.log( info ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
console.log( ALPHA ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
console.log( BETA ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
```

</section>

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `DTGSJA`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

DTGSJA computes the generalized singular value decomposition (GSVD) of two real upper triangular (or trapezoidal) matrices A and B.

On entry, it is assumed that matrices A and B have the following forms, which may be obtained by the preprocessing subroutine DGGSVP from a general M-by-N matrix A and P-by-N matrix B:

```text
          N-K-L  K    L
A =    K ( 0    A12  A13 ) if M-K-L >= 0;
       L ( 0     0   A23 )
   M-K-L ( 0     0    0  )
```

```text
        N-K-L  K    L
A =  K ( 0    A12  A13 ) if M-K-L < 0;
   M-K ( 0     0   A23 )
```

```text
        N-K-L  K    L
B =  L ( 0     0   B13 )
   P-L ( 0     0    0  )
```

where the K-by-K matrix A12 and L-by-L matrix B13 are nonsingular upper triangular; A23 is L-by-L upper triangular if $M-K-L \ge 0$, otherwise A23 is (M-K)-by-L upper trapezoidal.

On exit,

$$
U^T \, A \, Q = D_{1} \, ( 0 R ), V^T \, B \, Q = D_{2} \, ( 0 R )
$$

where U, V and Q are orthogonal matrices. R is a nonsingular upper triangular matrix, and D1 and D2 are \`\`diagonal'' matrices, which are of the following structures:

If $M-K-L \ge 0$,

```text
             K  L
D1 =     K ( I  0 )
         L ( 0  C )
     M-K-L ( 0  0 )
```

```text
           K  L
D2 = L   ( 0  S )
     P-L ( 0  0 )
```

```text
             N-K-L  K    L
( 0 R ) = K (  0   R11  R12 ) K
          L (  0    0   R22 ) L
```

where

$$
C = \operatorname{diag}( \mathrm{ALPHA}(K+1), \cdots , \mathrm{ALPHA}(K+L) )
$$

$$
S = \operatorname{diag}( \mathrm{BETA}(K+1), \cdots , \mathrm{BETA}(K+L) )
$$

$$
C^2 + S^2 = I
$$

R is stored in `A(1:K+L,N-K-L+1:N)` on exit.

If $M-K-L < 0$,

```text
           K M-K K+L-M
D1 =   K ( I  0    0   )
     M-K ( 0  C    0   )
```

```text
             K M-K K+L-M
D2 =   M-K ( 0  S    0   )
     K+L-M ( 0  0    I   )
       P-L ( 0  0    0   )
```

```text
               N-K-L  K   M-K  K+L-M
( 0 R ) =    K ( 0    R11  R12  R13  )
          M-K ( 0     0   R22  R23  )
        K+L-M ( 0     0    0   R33  )
```

where $C = \operatorname{diag}( \mathrm{ALPHA}(K+1), \cdots , \mathrm{ALPHA}(M) )$, $S = \operatorname{diag}( \mathrm{BETA}(K+1), \cdots , \mathrm{BETA}(M) )$, $C^2 + S^2 = I$.

$R = ( R_{11} R_{12} R_{13} )$ is stored in A(1:M, N-K-L+1:N) and R33 is stored

( 0 R22 R23 )

in `B(M-K+1:L,N+M-K-L+1:N)` on exit.

The computation of the orthogonal transformation matrices U, V or Q is optional. These matrices may either be formed explicitly, or they may be postmultiplied into input matrices U1, V1, or Q1.

### Further Details

DTGSJA essentially uses a variant of Kogbetliantz algorithm to reduce min(L,M-K)-by-L triangular (or trapezoidal) matrix A23 and L-by-L matrix B13 to the form:

$$
U_{1}^T \, A_{13} \, Q_{1} = C_{1} \, R_{1}; V_{1}^T \, B_{13} \, Q_{1} = S_{1} \, R_{1}
$$

where U1, V1 and Q1 are orthogonal matrix, and $Z^T$ is the transpose of Z. C1 and S1 are diagonal matrices satisfying

$$
C_{1}^2 + S_{1}^2 = I
$$

and R1 is an L-by-L nonsingular upper triangular matrix.

</section>
